title: Equivariant represented right torsors and restriction isomorphisms
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $G,H$ be group objects over $B$ with the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $S$ be a $B$-scheme with a specified left $G$-action. An equivariant represented right $H$-torsor is a represented right $H$-torsor $p:P\to S$ in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors], together with a left $G$-action on $P$ covering the specified action on $S$ and commuting with the right $H$-action. Thus on every test $B$-scheme $T$, $p(gx)=g p(x)$ and $g(xh)=(gx)h$. For $B$-schemes $S,V$ with specified $G$-actions, an equivariant map $j:S\to V$, such a torsor $P$ over $S$ and such a torsor $Q$ over $V$, an equivariant restriction isomorphism is a $B$-map $f:P\to Q$ for which the square with $p_P,p_Q,j$ is cartesian and which preserves both the left $G$-action and the right $H$-action on every test scheme. This identifies $P$ with $j^*Q$ as an equivariant right torsor, equivalently $j^*Q\simeq P$. For $j=\operatorname{id}$ these are equivariant torsor isomorphisms.

source.place: Author-hosted https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf; Section 2, Claims 1--2, printed p.2; Section 3, Theorem 1.3 (1) implies (2), printed p.6.
